src-tauri/src/agent_console/commands.rs:347-389 creates a fresh registry session for every resume_agent_journal_session invocation before returning its result.
findings.impact: resume_agent_journal_session starts and registers a new provider session on each invocation. If the first invoke loses its response after starting the process, the frontend can invoke it up to five times, leaving duplicate or orphaned sessions before any user turn is sent and violating idempotent resume/at-most-once recovery.
findings.observation: The resumed write now restricts replay to session_not_running, but resumeAgentJournalSession is still invoked through recover(), whose default retry policy retries unclassified failures.
findings.recommendation: Do not automatically retry the resume command after an unclassified/ambiguous failure; keep the pending draft and require inspection before a user initiated retry. Add a regression where resume rejects with an unclassified error after its side effect and assert one resume invocation and no write dispatch.

Add a running/waiting regression that asserts both status surfaces communicate readiness consistently.

findings.impact: A known session_not_running, invalid_input, or attachment validation failure is presented as No se pudo confirmar el envío and asks the user to inspect the conversation, even though the backend has rejected it before dispatch. The message hides the actionable recovery path and makes safe retries look ambiguous.
findings.observation: The catch block now uses the ambiguous-response message for every send error, including categorized failures known to occur before provider dispatch.
findings.recommendation: Choose the alert copy from the error category: preserve the inspect-before-resend warning only for unclassified/ambiguous failures, while known pre-dispatch categories retain a direct retry or correction message. Cover at least session_not_running and attachment validation in focused tests.
